revisions.title: The measured marvel: canals, temple, and rings of trust
revisions.body: The description compresses the capital into an ordered scale: canals and concentric rings organize the city, while temple, royal precinct, baths, hippodrome, and docks distribute sacred, civic, and practical functions. The graded placement of guards toward the acropolis turns the layout into a hierarchy of trust. Critias closes by marking the account as approximate.

revisions.title: When wealth changes meaning
revisions.body: Wealth is first described as light because the divine element governs its use; as that element fades into mortal mixture, the same abundance becomes a burden. The passage then contrasts genuine happiness with the ambition and power that appear blessed to those unable to recognize the difference. Zeus sees the race's wretched condition and calls the gods together.
